pr.title: Add `#[optimize(none)]`
pr.description:
cc #54882

This extends the `optimize` attribute to add `none`, which corresponds to the LLVM `OptimizeNone` attribute.

Not sure if an MCP is required for this, happy to file one if so.
pr.author: clubby789

processing.reason: PR #128657 introduces the `#[optimize(none)]` attribute as a per-function optimization-control feature: it emits LLVM `optnone`+`noinline` and passes `Optimizations::Suppressed` so non-required MIR passes are skipped. The historically wrong transformation described by the PR is treating `#[optimize(none)]` like the old `OptimizeAttr::None`/absence path (or implementing only the LLVM attribute), which leaves non-required MIR optimizations enabled. That transformation changes only whether semantics-preserving MIR/unoptimized codegen passes run; it does not change the defined runtime result of the function. The PR's own MIR tests demonstrate exactly this: `1 + 2` is retained as `AddWithOverflow(const 1, const 2); assert` under `#[optimize(none)]` but folded to `const 3` otherwise, and `if true { 1 } else { 0 }` retains a `switchInt` branch but both paths still return the same value. Likewise the codegen test just checks that an `alloca` and `optnone`/`noinline` attributes remain. There is no source-grounded concrete input for which suppressing these optional optimization passes changes the program's observable numeric/boolean/character result; manufacturing such a divergence (e.g. by inventing a different computation or exploiting unrelated unsoundness) would not encode the actual historical rewrite. Since both candidate functions must pass Miri and produce different defined values, no valid `test_program_pair` counterexample exists for this optimization-only PR.

analysis.summary: This is a feature/optimization PR, not a confirmed bug fix. It adds `#[optimize(none)]` as a distinct `OptimizeAttr::DoNotOptimize`, emits LLVM `optnone` plus `noinline`, and makes `run_optimization_passes` pass `Optimizations::Suppressed` so non-required MIR passes are skipped while required/soundness passes still run. Source and test inspection only; no compiler was built or executed.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `OptimizeAttr` had only `None`/`Speed`/`Size`; `None` meant "no `optimize` attribute" and was also the parser fallback for missing or invalid arguments. `llfn_attrs_from_instance` mapped `OptimizeAttr::None` to default optimisation attributes, and `should_run_pass` decided solely from an explicit `-Zmir-enable-pass` override or `pass.is_enabled(tcx.sess)`. The builtin attribute template accepted only `size|speed`, so there was no per-function way to keep non-required MIR optimizations from running.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, treating `#[optimize(none)]` as the old `OptimizeAttr::None`/absence path (or implementing only an LLVM attribute) would leave non-required MIR optimizations such as constant folding and branch simplification enabled, and would omit the required LLVM `optnone`/`noinline` pair. The old `None` variant cannot be reused for `none` because it also represents "no attribute". The corrected design adds a separate `DoNotOptimize`, filters `!pass.is_required()` only when `Optimizations::Suppressed`, and emits `OptimizeNone` with forced `InlineAttr::Never`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions compiled with `#![feature(optimize_attribute)]`. Compare a function annotated `#[optimize(none)]` against the same body with no `optimize` attribute, or against `#[optimize(speed)]`/`#[optimize(size)]`. Exercise both `-Copt-level=0` and `-Copt-level=3 -Coverflow-checks=y`, with bodies such as checked integer addition and `if true { 1 } else { 0 }`; include a `#[no_mangle]` function for codegen attribute inspection. Avoid `-Zmir-enable-pass` overrides when testing suppression.
analysis.trigger: A function with codegen attrs is annotated `#[optimize(none)]`, causing `codegen_fn_attrs.optimize` to be `DoNotOptimize`. During `run_optimization_passes`, the body's own `def_id` selects `Optimizations::Suppressed`; during codegen, `llfn_attrs_from_instance` emits LLVM `OptimizeNone` and forces `noinline`.
preconditions: The annotated item is function-like and has codegen attrs: `tcx.def_kind(def_id).has_codegen_attrs()` is checked before reading `codegen_fn_attrs`.
The body reaches `run_optimization_passes`; other pipelines still call `run_passes(..., Optimizations::Allowed)`, so `optimize(none)` is not a global compiler-wide optimization switch.
For LLVM checks, codegen the annotated function and inspect emitted attributes; for MIR checks, use `tests/mir-opt` expectations rather than explicitly enabling individual passes.
pitfalls: Do not equate `#[optimize(none)]` with `-Copt-level=0`: suppression is a per-body MIR optimization filter, and required passes still run.
`optnone` requires `noinline`; codegen forces `InlineAttr::Never` for `DoNotOptimize`, even when `#[inline(always)]` or `requires_inline` would otherwise produce an inline hint.

Suppression is computed from `body.source.def_id()`, not from callee attributes. Annotate the function whose MIR you expect to be suppressed; this patch alone does not establish a callee-level barrier for the caller's `Inline` pass.
`-Zmir-enable-pass` overrides suppression because `overridden.unwrap_or_else(...)` is evaluated first. Tests of `optimize(none)` must not explicitly enable the pass they expect to be suppressed.

`OptimizeAttr::Default` means the absence of the attribute; only `DoNotOptimize` triggers suppression and `optnone`. Invalid or missing `optimize` arguments fall back to `Default`, not `DoNotOptimize`.

Required passes such as `AbortUnwindingCalls`, `AddCallGuards`, `ElaborateDrops`, `LowerIntrinsics`, `StateTransform`, `PromoteTemps`, `Validator`, and `ForceInline` remain enabled under `Optimizations::Suppressed`; expect neither completely untouched MIR nor absence of forced inlining.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/optimize_none.rs` style revisions: `NO-OPT` = `-Copt-level=0`; `SPEED-OPT` = `-Copt-level=3 -Coverflow-checks=y`. For `#[optimize(none)] fn add_noopt() -> i32 { 1 + 2 }`, expect MIR to retain `AddWithOverflow(const 1_i32, const 2_i32);` followed by `assert`, rather than folding to `const 3`. For `#[optimize(none)] fn const_branch() -> i32 { if true { 1 } else { 0 } }`, expect `switchInt(const true) -> [0: [[FALSE]], otherwise: [[TRUE]]]` with both blocks assigning 0/1, rather than collapsing the branch. For codegen, add `#[no_mangle] #[optimize(none)] pub fn none()` and check `attributes [[NONE_ATTRS]] = {{.*}}noinline{{.*}}optnone{{.*}}`; also check `alloca` remains in the `SIZE-OPT`/`SPEED-OPT` revisions as in `tests/codegen/optimize-attr-1.rs`. Update the feature-gate UI so `#[optimize(none)]` is gated, and update the builtin template to `none|size|speed`.
